If a customer abandons checkout, their seats stay held (blocked in inventory) for up to ten minutes; a background worker scanning every 30 seconds then lapses the unpaid hold, returns the seats to inventory, and invalidates the event page cache (any late payment on a lapsed hold triggers an automatic refund).

When a customer starts checkout, `tide-web` places a hold on the chosen seats via `POST /holds`; if payment isn't completed, `tide-worker` scans holds every 30 seconds and lets unpaid holds lapse after 10 minutes, returning the seats to inventory and invalidating the event page cache (a late Paylane confirmation on an already-lapsed hold triggers an automatic refund).

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-04-01-hold-release-worker.md, tidewater/plans/2026-01-25-checkout-flow.md

Entry validation (Gatekeeper) consumes each QR token atomically via `UPDATE entries SET consumed_at = now() WHERE token = $1 AND consumed_at IS NULL`, so a second scan at any gate fails and shows "already used" with the time/gate of the first entry (this fixed BUG-017's race condition); offline gates keep a local consumed list that reconciles later, with conflicts flagged in the venue report.

To undo a broken schema change in production, run `tidectl migrate --env prod --down 1` to apply the paired `.down.sql` of the last migration; if that migration dropped or rewrote data, the down file can't restore it, so you must instead restore the Postgres backup to the moment before it ran.

Sources: tidewater/skills/run-db-migration.md, tidewater/memory/conventions.md

To undo a broken schema change in prod, run `tidectl migrate --env prod --down 1` to apply the last migration's paired `.down.sql`; if the migration dropped/rewrote data (so the down file can't restore it), instead restore Postgres to the point before the change via the restore-postgres-backup skill.

Sources: tidewater/skills/run-db-migration.md

TLS certificates for tidewater.example are renewed automatically via certbot (DNS challenge) on a systemd timer every 12 hours, with a deploy hook that rebuilds the HAProxy cert bundle and reloads it without dropping connections; if that fails, the manual fallback is `sudo certbot renew --cert-name tidewater.example --force-renewal` on kelp-1, then rebuild the HAProxy bundle and `systemctl reload haproxy`.

Sources: tidewater/plans/2026-05-18-automazione-tls.md, tidewater/skills/rinnovo-certificati-tls.md

Certificates (Let's Encrypt, valid 90 days) auto-renew every 60 days via certbot's timer; if that fails and expiry is within 14 days, run the manual procedure on `kelp-1`: `sudo certbot renew --cert-name tidewater.example --force-renewal`, verify with `openssl x509 -enddate`, rebuild the HAProxy bundle (`haproxy-cert-bundle`), then `systemctl reload haproxy` and confirm with `curl -vI`.

Sources: tidewater/skills/rinnovo-certificati-tls.md, tidewater/plans/2026-05-18-automazione-tls.md

Each entry token is consumed atomically via a single conditional SQL update (`UPDATE entries SET consumed_at = now() WHERE token = $1 AND consumed_at IS NULL`), so only the first scan at any gate succeeds; any later attempt gets "already used" with the time/gate of the original entry, and offline gates reconcile afterward with conflicts routed to a venue report.

Tickets use single-use QR entry tokens; Gatekeeper's validation call consumes the token atomically (`UPDATE entries SET consumed_at = now() WHERE token = $1 AND consumed_at IS NULL`), so a second scan at any gate fails with "already used" plus the time/gate of the first scan — this fixed a race (BUG-017) where two gates could validate the same QR simultaneously.
